note: Every recipe carries executable checks. tests/knowledge_checks.py compiles each with the pinned compiler through tools/probe.py: 'exact' checks must match the pinned original bytes and 'differs' checks must not. A recipe whose checks fail is stale; fix or retire it, never loosen the check. Exact bytes do not prove source types or the original author's code.

statuses.verifier-proved: The lever produced current exact proofs through scripts/verify.
statuses.probe-observed: Reproducible with tools/probe.py but not yet behind a published proof.
statuses.toolchain-limited: A family with zero exact proofs and a reviewed negative search under this toolchain.

recipes.title: Operand order, register choice and schedule follow internal symbol numbering
recipes.symptom: Candidate has the target's instructions but `cmp ecx, eax` vs `cmp eax, ecx` (with the mirrored jcc), SIB base/index swapped, a different register, or one independent instruction moved.
recipes.action: Leave the body alone. Run tools/perturb.py ADDRESS SOURCE --moves: it first tries every order of up to five top-level declarations (else single moves and swaps), then inserts 1-16 unused `extern int decl_pad_N;` data declarations at each declaration slot. Publish the first exact variant with scripts/verify.

checks.why: global declared before the callee: cmp operands in the wrong order
one unused declaration first is not enough
two unused declarations first flip the compare; names and data types do not matter
a pure instruction-schedule difference fixed by padding alone

caveats: Padding is compiler-state reproduction, not recovered source; keep the comment block the tool writes.
Function prototypes perturb numbering differently from data declarations; use data declarations.
Rename-only changes of any identifier do nothing.
Counts above eight matter: 00429b40 needed 10 and 00433590 needed 14.

recipes.title: Reordering existing declarations is the same lever without padding; a commutative sum follows declaration order
recipes.symptom: As symbol-numbering-padding.
recipes.action: tools/perturb.py --moves tries every single move and swap of the top-level declarations. Prefer this when it works: the source stays free of padding.

checks.why: callee declared before the global
four globals summed in a loop load in the reverse of their declaration order

caveats: 96 semantic C++ variants of 0042dcf0 (docs/compiler-guided-search.md) never moved this; the decisive change was outside the function body.
Source term order in a + b + c + d is canonicalised; only the declaration order moved it (004237c0 needed the exact reverse, one of 24 orders).

recipes.title: /Tc (C) and /Tp (C++) number symbols differently
recipes.symptom: As symbol-numbering-padding, when padding and moves under the contract language fail.
recipes.action: tools/perturb.py --languages cpp,c. A C result needs functionOverrides[address].language = "c" in project.json, which is a configuration change (service restart). Prefer a C++ perturbation when one exists: 004195d0 and 004404b0 matched both ways.

checks.why: the C++-failing declaration order matches under /Tc

caveats: 441 of 452 comparable exact C++ proofs also match under a mechanical C conversion; the language is another perturbation, not evidence the game was C++ or C.

recipes.title: Write fields the way the programmer did, through the pointer, with real member names
recipes.symptom: Ghidra-shaped source (`int a = p[0x25]; int b = p[0x23]; ... p[0x23] = sum`) compiles to the right instructions with compares or loads in another order. Also: Ghidra's goto form of nested if/else produces an inverted conditional jump plus an extra jmp.
recipes.action: Get the layout with tools/ghidra_struct.py GXObject --only <offsets>, then write `gob->gob_yVel += gob->gob_yAccl; if (gob->gob_yVel > gob->gob_maxyVel) ...` re-reading fields instead of caching them in locals.

checks.why: Ghidra's goto-shaped clamp inverted one branch; the natural if/else-if with re-read fields matched first try
the retained candidate used a volatile read to force a load order; plain field access matched first try

caveats: Ghidra types GXObject parameters as GXObject**; that is an analysis error, not a clue.

recipes.title: A different `sub esp, N` means a local aggregate of the wrong size, not a scheduling issue
recipes.symptom: Frame size and every [esp+k] displacement differ while the instructions match. Ghidra split one out-parameter buffer into `local_28[6]`, `local_10`, `local_c` (the last two never written in source), so the compiler lays out a smaller frame.
recipes.action: Size the buffer from `sub esp, N` and the lea passed to the callee, then read fields as elements of that one buffer (00421820: int edges[10], reading edges[6] and edges[7]).
caveats: Reading a Ghidra-named local that the source never assigns is undefined behaviour and a sign of this split.

recipes.title: `and r, 0x80000000` + `shr r, 0x1c` is a ternary `flags & 0x80000000 ? 8 : 0`
recipes.symptom: Target keeps the narrow mask `and edi, 0x80000000` before `shr edi, 0x1c` (bit 31 to bit 3); a shift or divide in the candidate compiles to `and edi, 0x8fffffff` instead. `and r, 0x80000000; shr r, 0x1f` is the same idiom with 1/0.
recipes.action: Write the flip bit as a ternary: `(flags & 0x80000000 ? 8 : 0) | angle >> 21` (the direction index of the InitPlayerSide* family). CL 10.00 lowers a select between a power of two and 0 to mask+shift and keeps the narrow mask. For the 1/0 form write `(flags & 0x80000000) != 0`. tools/idiom_scan.py still lists candidates; they are source shapes, not a toolchain limit.

checks.why: (flags & 0x80000000) >> 28 widens the mask to 0x8fffffff

caveats: Every shift, divide and bitfield spelling widens (>> 28) or drops (>> 31) the mask; only the ternary (or != 0) keeps it. Found 2026-09-26 from 004207e0, whose `(x & 0x80000000) != 0` already compiled to and/shr 0x1f.

recipes.title: Bodies that end in call _exit: two different problems
recipes.symptom: Recorded extent ends in `call _exit`. For 00436c90 the original continues `add esp, 4; ret` right after: Ghidra assumed _exit is noreturn and cut the extent, so the verifier refuses a body that is actually complete (an extent bug, and a candidate compiles to exactly those bytes). For 004064d0 and 00449bd0 the original really has no epilogue, which CL 10.00 cannot produce.
recipes.action: 00436c90: needs an extent repair in the backend (extend a call-terminated extent through the following epilogue when no function starts inside). The other two: skip.
caveats: 00402ec0 (MUS_SetMusicPlaying) also calls _exit mid-function and continues normally, so the original compiler did not treat _exit as noreturn everywhere.

recipes.title: A higher positional score can come from wrong semantics
recipes.symptom: 0042de50's retained best (93.9%) passes its two parameters to both callees swapped; that happens to reproduce the target's esi/edi assignment. The semantically correct source scores 81.8% and no perturbation found tried so far flips its registers.
recipes.action: Before perturbing or keeping a best candidate, check argument order against the target's push sequence. Never keep a higher-scoring source that computes something else.

checks.why: correct argument order, registers still swapped

caveats: The loop's monotonic best-score preservation will keep the wrong source; this needs a semantic check the backend does not have.

recipes.title: Switches: the jump table follows the code; the verifier now compares it
recipes.symptom: Candidate is longer than the recorded extent by the table size; before loop-trailing-data every such function plateaued near 93%.
recipes.action: Write a normal switch. pc-decomp (switch-tables backend) widens the comparison to referenced trailing data when no other function starts inside it; tools/probe.py does the same.

checks.why: 31 table bytes past the extent

caveats: Seven of these sources were already byte-exact; only the extent rule had hidden it.

recipes.title: Flags polled across threads were volatile
recipes.symptom: Target keeps constant 0 in a callee-saved register (`xor edi, edi` ... `push edi` for Sleep(0)) and reloads a flag every iteration; candidate pushes an immediate.
recipes.action: Declare the polled globals `volatile` (tools/perturb.py --volatile tries every subset).
caveats: Only the flags the loop polls: 0040b320 needed exactly gFreezeGame and M1_004a2a84.

recipes.title: Independent statement order and local declaration-list order move scheduling and registers
recipes.symptom: Same instructions, one store or call placed differently, or two locals' registers swapped.
recipes.action: Permute adjacent statements (including calls) and the names in `int a, b;` lists. Exact bytes prove the reordering equivalent, so no independence analysis is needed.

checks.why: `int count, i;` rather than `int i, count;`

caveats: Stack slot assignment for aggregates did not follow declaration order (004044b0).

recipes.title: `(x & 0x80000000) != 0` keeps `and; shr 31`
recipes.symptom: Target `and eax, 0x80000000; shr eax, 0x1f`; `x >> 31` drops the mask.
recipes.action: Write the test form `(x & 0x80000000) != 0`.
caveats: The narrow-mask-shift family is solved by the ternary form (see that recipe).

recipes.title: `int 3` after OutputDebugString needs inline assembly (refused by policy)
recipes.symptom: Function has an ebp frame and an `int3` after an error message (CDIO_FileClose, FreeMemory).
recipes.action: Skip: sources may not contain inline assembly and VC4 has no __debugbreak.

recipes.title: Absolute value shape follows the source form
recipes.symptom: Target has `mov eax, x; jns; mov eax, x; neg eax` where the candidate has `cdq; xor; sub` (or the reverse).
recipes.action: `if (x < 0) d = -x; else d = x;` gives the branch; `x < 0 ? -x : x` gives cdq/xor/sub.

checks.why: if/else abs gives mov/jns/mov/neg
ternary abs gives cdq/xor/sub

recipes.title: DirectX COM calls are C style
recipes.symptom: `call dword ptr [eax + N]` on a DirectX object with the `this` push scheduled differently.
recipes.action: Declare a C vtable struct and call `obj->lpVtbl->Method(obj, ...)`, not a C++ virtual interface.

checks.why: obj->lpVtbl->Method(obj, ...)
C++ virtual __stdcall interface schedules the this-push differently

recipes.title: Blocks are laid out in source order
recipes.symptom: The target keeps an error path (or one branch) at the end of the function, the candidate inline.
recipes.action: Make the out-of-line body the `else` branch: `if (ok) { ... } else error();`.

checks.why: if (ok) {...} else error(): error path at the end
early-return error path is laid out inline

recipes.title: Common code after an if/else is tail-duplicated
recipes.symptom: One store appears in both branches with an immediate while neighbouring stores in the branch reuse a register.
recipes.action: Move that statement after the if/else.

checks.why: shared store after the if/else, duplicated by the compiler with an immediate
the store written in both branches reuses a register

recipes.title: Explicit empty case labels keep the jump table bound
recipes.symptom: Only the jump-table bound (`cmp eax, N`) differs.
recipes.action: List every empty case up to the target bound with `break;`; a single empty case is dropped.

checks.why: all empty cases listed keep the 10-entry jump table
a lone empty case 10 is dropped and the table shrinks

recipes.title: Duplicate case bodies merge into the later block
recipes.symptom: Two table slots share one block that sits after higher cases.
recipes.action: Write the two cases with separate identical bodies instead of stacked labels.

checks.why: separate identical bodies merge into the later block
'case 0xc: case 0x70:' places the block at 0xc's position

recipes.title: Per-branch struct copies are cross-jumped
recipes.symptom: Each branch loads a source address into esi and jumps to one `rep movsd`.
recipes.action: Write one struct assignment per branch rather than selecting a pointer and copying once.

checks.why: one struct assignment per branch; the rep movsd tail is cross-jumped
pointer chosen by if/else then one copy becomes a speculative assignment

recipes.title: Down-counted loops come from stepped for loops
recipes.symptom: A trip count like `(n + 7) >> 3` feeds a `dec; jne` loop.
recipes.action: `for (n = 0; n < bits; n += 8)`; the compiler computes the trip count.

checks.why: for (n = 0; n < bits; n += 8) with an int key
unsigned char key keeps byte arithmetic

recipes.title: Script readers use post-increment
recipes.symptom: `inc esi` twice before reading `[esi-2]` and `[esi-1]`.
recipes.action: `a = *p++; b = *p++;` instead of indexed reads and one `p += 2`.

checks.why: *script++ twice: inc esi; inc esi; [esi-2], [esi-1]
script[0], script[1]; script += 2

recipes.title: Writes through a just-stored global pointer
recipes.symptom: Absolute `and [X], m` right after `ptr = &X`, and an unrelated char global reloaded afterwards.
recipes.action: Write through the pointer (`*ptr &= m`), not to X directly.

checks.why: write through the just-stored global pointer: absolute and + reload of the char global
writing the target directly lets the compiler keep the char in a register

recipes.title: Ghidra's &obj->field locals are compiler CSE
recipes.symptom: A `lea reg, [obj + off]` reused for a field, with the candidate's schedule slightly off.
recipes.action: Access `obj->field` directly; drop Ghidra's pointer local.

checks.why: plain file->offset; the lea is the compiler CSE
Ghidra's int *p = &file->offset local changes the schedule

recipes.title: Error paths join one return
recipes.symptom: Error paths return `mov eax, esi` although the variable is known to be 0.
recipes.action: Jump (goto or fall-through) to one `return var;`; separate returns fold to `xor eax, eax`.

checks.why: error paths jump to the common return: mov eax, esi is kept
return frame; in each error path constant-folds to xor eax, eax

recipes.title: mov reg, 0 marks a ternary
recipes.symptom: `mov reg, 0` (not `xor`) set before a test and conditional overwrite.
recipes.action: Write `v = cond ? a : 0;`.

checks.why: x ? a : 0 gives mov reg, 0 before the test
if-assign gives xor and a register compare

recipes.title: Small memset zero fills use a zero register
recipes.symptom: `xor reg, reg` then several register stores into one struct.
recipes.action: `memset(p, 0, sizeof *p)` (intrinsic under /O2; never with a pragma).

checks.why: memset of a small struct: xor reg then register stores
field-by-field zeroing stores immediates

recipes.title: `mov ah, byte ptr [reg + off + 1]; test ah, k` is `(unsigned char)(x >> 8) & k`
recipes.symptom: Target loads one byte of a dword field straight into AH and tests it; the candidate loads the dword (`mov eax, [reg + off]; test ah, k`) or puts the byte in AL.
recipes.action: Cast the shifted field: `(unsigned char)(gob->flags2 >> 8) & 8` for bit 11. A mask, a bitfield, a `(char *)` byte access or a `short` view of the field all compile differently.

checks.why: flags2 & 0x800 loads the whole dword

caveats: Listed as a toolchain limit until 2026-09-27; see toolchain-limits.md.

recipes.title: `mov edx, ecx; and edx, ecx` into a just-written global is PSX `setlen(p, 0)` through a tag pointer
recipes.symptom: A global is stored with a register holding 0xffffff, then stored again with that register ANDed with itself; the candidate folds the AND away (direct `&=`) or reloads the global (store through the pointer).
recipes.action: The code is a port of PSX libgpu ordering-table macros. Declare `struct Tag { unsigned addr : 24; unsigned len : 8; };` and clear the length through the list pointer that was just assigned: `((struct Tag *)DAT_0046bc6c)->len = 0;` after the direct stores of 0xffffff (termPrim).

checks.why: a direct &= 0xffffff is constant-folded and the store dropped

caveats: Related to store-through-global-pointer (0043daf0), which is the same macro family written as an int &=.

recipes.title: `mov eax, [g]; mov [m], 1; test; jne; mov [m], 0` is `if (g) m = 1; else m = 0;`
recipes.symptom: The original loads the condition, stores the then-constant to memory before the test, and overwrites with the else-constant on the fall-through; the candidate loads the condition after the first store.
recipes.action: Write both arms: `if (g) m = 1; else m = 0;`. CL 10.00 emits the then-store ahead of the test with the condition load first. Writing `m = 1; if (!g) m = 0;` keeps the store first and the load after it. In an if/else-if chain, give each arm its own if/else; the identical stores are cross-jumped (`test; je zero; jmp one`).

checks.why: m = 1; if (!g) m = 0; loads the global after the first store

caveats: Only for a memory destination; a register result uses setcc or sbb instead.
